review_notes: I read the whole target file. I also read GroupLikeHom.lean to see which simp lemmas exist (map_val, map_id, map_comp, coalgHomEquiv_apply, coalgHomEquiv_symm_val). I looked at the downstream users: the Bialgebra tensorMulEquiv and the test file. I did not look for loops: the lemmas tensorEquiv_apply_fst, tensorEquiv_apply_snd and tensorEquiv_symm_val rewrite in a terminating direction. I could not run Lean, so I don't know what the simp set does with `GroupLike.map πC x` and `.val` in practice. The suggestions below are therefore about missing interface lemmas, and none has been compiled.

findings.excerpt: (tensorEquiv R C D x).1 = GroupLike.map πC x := rfl
findings.problem: The simp lemmas for the forward map rewrite to `GroupLike.map` of a composite `CoalgHom` (rid ∘ map id counit). There is no value-level lemma saying what `(tensorEquiv R C D x).1.val` is. The simp lemma `map_val` turns the result into an application of the composite, which has no simp-normal form of its own. The file's own proofs have to `change` through the composite by hand. The downstream test (AlgebraicGroupsTest/.../GroupLikeTensorProduct.lean, `tensorEquiv_subsingleton_scalar_contract`) states `(GroupLike.tensorEquiv R C D x).1.val = 0` and avoids computing it by using `Module.eq_zero_of_zero_eq_one`. So the `.val` of a decomposition has no usable simp form. Pure tensors are the only case with a natural form. For those, `tensorEquiv_apply_eq_iff` is a non-simp iff that rewrites nothing automatically.
findings.proposed_change: Add a lemma giving the applied form of the composite on pure tensors, e.g. `πC (c ⊗ₜ d) = Coalgebra.counit d • c` (and the `πD` analogue `= Coalgebra.counit c • d`). Mark it `@[simp]` or `private`, as appropriate. Then add a value lemma such as `(tensorEquiv R C D x).1.val = πC x.val`, or a `@[simp]` lemma for `(tensorEquiv R C D ((tensorEquiv R C D).symm (c, d))).1`. Together these let `simp` reduce both components of a decomposition to counit-scaled values. Keep the existing `rfl` lemmas.
findings.benefit: Users and later files can compute the components of a decomposition with `simp`. They would no longer need `change` or the unfolding of `map` and a composite coalgebra homomorphism.

findings.excerpt: change Coalgebra.counit (R := R) p.2.val • p.1.val = p.1.val
findings.problem: The file never states an apply or `tmul` simp lemma for the projection composites `πC` and `πD`. Four proofs (right_inv in both components, and both naturality components) reach the formula `counit d • c` only through `change` with an explicit definitional unfolding. Examples are `change Coalgebra.counit (R := R) (g d) • f c = f (...)` and `change πC (((1 : R) • p.1.val) ⊗ₜ ...)`. This pattern is repeated four times. It depends on defeq of the `rid`, `map` and `counitCoalgHom` composite, and `simp` cannot discharge these steps. A single lemma `πC (c ⊗ₜ d) = counit d • c` is the canonical normal form and is missing.
findings.proposed_change: Introduce (possibly private) lemmas `πC (c ⊗ₜ[R] d) = Coalgebra.counit (R := R) d • c` and `πD (c ⊗ₜ[R] d) = Coalgebra.counit (R := R) c • d`, proved once by `rfl`. Tag them `@[simp]` or use them with `simp only`. Replace the repeated `change ... ; rw [...]` blocks with `simp only [πC_tmul, ...]`.
findings.benefit: The unfolding is stated once and checked once. The right_inv and naturality proofs become short `simp`/`rw` calls instead of repeated `change` blocks. The proofs also no longer break if the definition of the projection composite is refactored.
